messages:
maria: Quick idea — instead of repeating the full metadata blob in every shard header, stripe detailed metadata blocks across shards and keep a tiny inline summary in each shard for hotload. Cuts header bloat. Thoughts?
cheng: Striping reduces per-shard header size, nice. Tradeoff is more fanout for metadata reads during warmup. How do we avoid extra round-trips for SLO-critical requests?
oliver: We can parallelize a lightweight metadata-merge pass during prefetch. Important: each striped block needs a checksum and version so we can detect corruption/rollbacks.
maria: Agreed on checksums. Proposal: per-block CRC32 + schema version. Also add a tiny per-shard 'metadata bloom' (bitmap) to quickly test presence of blocks without fetching them.
sasha: Concern about tail latency — if the summary points to block idxs that live on other shards and one of those is slow, we get an extra hop. Maybe keep a small fixed-size inline summary (128 bytes) with offsets + a warmup-order hint so we minimize extra fetches.
cheng: Yes — inline summary (fixed 128B) + striped detail blocks. Summary fields: model_id, format_version, block_count, compact fingerprint, primary warmup hint, per-shard preferred reader flag.
oliver: API boundary thought: weightsource should expose two cheap calls: `get_metadata_summary(shard_id)` and `fetch_block(shard_id, block_idx)`. Keep it stream-friendly so transports can optimize.
maria: Backward compatibility: old loaders will read only the summary and fall back to legacy warmup if they don't understand striping. We need a manifestless resolver that can probe support.
infra-bot: deploy-bot: canary for loader-api-v2 scheduled: 2025-06-12 16:00 UTC :rocket:
sasha: Some rough perf numbers to keep in mind — summary read local disk ~0.2ms, network block fetch ~1–5ms per block. So we should design to minimize cross-shard block fetches on the critical path.
cheng: Proposed hotload procedure: 1) always read inline summary; 2) consult telemetry + warmup hint to choose top-k blocks and fetch them on-demand; 3) background-hydrate remainder asynchronously. Keeps tail low and bandwidth reasonable.
maria: Top-k selection should use historical prefix heatmap from telemetry. We could run a small model that suggests the first blocks to hydrate per route.
oliver: Implementation note: block fetch should support batching: `fetch_blocks([{shard, idx}, ...])` -> single RPC to reduce RTTs. Make sure it is idempotent and retryable.
sasha: Telemetry to record: block-miss-rate, avg extra latency per-request due to metadata fetches, bytes saved vs full header, and checksum-failure counts. Flag shards with repeated corruption.
maria: Test plan: unit tests for summary parser, integration simulating striping and single-shard failures, chaos tests dropping random block RPCs, and perf benchmarks. Also write a clear migration guide for older runtimes.
cheng: Question about compression: should striped blocks be zstd-compressed? Saves bandwidth at cost of CPU. Maybe negotiation per-device/region in the summary.
oliver: Make compression optional and negotiated in the summary; include compressed-size field and an algorithm tag. Add decompression benchmarks to runtime CI.
sasha: Security note: ensure the summary+blocks have a provenance signature for tamper detection (HMAC over summary + block fingerprints) so private deployments can verify integrity.
maria: Next steps: draft an RFC with API sketches, perf estimates, telemetry schema, and migration plan. Who wants to co-author?
maria: I'll start drafting. @cheng can you add telemetry schema? @oliver can you sketch the batched RPC interface?
cheng: I can add telemetry.
oliver: I'll draft the RPC/transport sketch.
sasha: I'll add the chaos tests and the security signature bits.
maria: sg — I'll file the RFC under docs/rfcs/ and link perf runs. Thanks all :thumbsup:
